planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade sheltered from strong sun and wind; the creamy leaf margins scorch readily in hot afternoon exposure, so a woodland-edge site with dappled light suits it best.

directions: Magpie is a variegated sport of early stachyurus, its arching branches carrying the same drooping chains of pale yellow, bell-shaped late-winter flowers but paired with oval leaves broadly edged in cream-white, the newest growth often flushed pink before settling into the mature two-tone pattern. It grows noticeably more slowly and stays more compact than the plain green species, making it a better fit for a smaller shaded border or container near a shaded patio where the bright foliage and winter bloom chains can be seen up close. Site it out of hot midday sun, which fades and scorches the variegated leaf margins, and out of harsh winter wind, which can desiccate the exposed cream tissue. Prune only immediately after flowering, since next winter's bloom buds form during the previous fall.
sources: Great Plant Picks (Elisabeth C. Miller Botanical Garden)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; Chinese stachyurus grows into a larger, more open shrub than the related Stachyurus praecox and needs more room to display its longer flower chains.

directions: Stachyurus chinensis is a larger, more vigorous relative of the better-known Stachyurus praecox, producing longer, more pendulous chains of pale yellow, bell-shaped flowers that open slightly later in the season, from early to mid spring rather than the depths of winter. Its arching, purplish-brown branches and glossy, tapering leaves give a graceful, fountain-like structure to a shaded border, and the extended flower racemes read as more dramatic than the shorter chains of its relative when viewed against bare late-winter branches. It shares the same preference for acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist soil favored by camellia and rhododendron, and appreciates protection from harsh winter wind and drying afternoon sun. Give it generous room, since it ultimately grows larger and more spreading than the more compact Stachyurus praecox.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Burnished Gold is a chartreuse-gold variegated selection of the plain-green Ternstroemia, brightening shaded foundation beds much like Jade Tiara but with a warmer gold tone rather than cream.

directions: Burnished Gold bears the same dense, glossy, leathery foliage and neat upright habit as the straight Ternstroemia species, but each leaf carries an irregular chartreuse-to-gold overlay rather than solid dark green, giving the shrub a warm, sunny presence even in the depths of a shaded border. Some direct morning or filtered sun deepens the gold coloring, while deeper shade shifts the leaves toward a softer yellow-green; either way, the plant retains the excellent shade tolerance of the species. Small, fragrant, creamy summer flowers and orange-red berries follow the same pattern as the plain form. It works well as a bright accent among darker evergreens or as an informal low screen, needing only occasional shaping and essentially no pest or disease management once established.

common_name: Big Bronze Ternstroemia (Large Bronze-Red New Growth Cleyera)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Big Bronze is a larger-leaved, larger-growing selection of Ternstroemia chosen for its exceptionally showy bronze-red new growth flushes.

directions: Big Bronze grows into a larger, more substantial shrub than the straight Ternstroemia species, with noticeably bigger, glossier leaves that emerge in dramatic flushes of deep wine-bronze before maturing to dark green, giving repeated seasonal color displays as new growth cycles through the year. Its bigger stature and denser habit make it an effective tall screen or background planting in a shaded border, standing in for evergreens like photinia or ligustrum where those are troubled by disease. Small, fragrant summer flowers and orange-red fall berries follow the same pattern as the species. It shares the excellent partial-to-full-shade tolerance, slow steady growth, and freedom from serious pests that make Ternstroemia valuable in shaded Southern landscapes, and needs little pruning beyond occasional shaping.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Gold Rush is valued in the specialty nursery trade for producing an unusually heavy set of flower buds, so a sheltered site with consistent moisture supports the best winter display.

directions: Gold Rush carries the same tiered, architectural branching and soft blue-green summer foliage as typical paperbush, but is selected for an especially heavy set of silvery winter flower buds that open into dense, rounded clusters of fragrant, tubular, rich gold flowers in late winter to earliest spring. The unusually abundant bud set makes for a fuller, more saturated floral display than seed-grown plants of the species, while requiring exactly the same care: humus-rich, evenly moist soil, shelter from harsh winter wind, and no pruning after midsummer once next winter's buds have begun forming. Site it near a path, entrance, or window where the strong fragrance and heavy late-winter bloom can be enjoyed at close range. It pairs well with early-blooming hellebores and hardy cyclamen at its base in a shaded winter garden.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / JLBG plant introductions

common_name: Pale Sweetshrub (Smooth Sweetshrub, Blue-Leaved Carolina Allspice)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs or rooted cuttings in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; this variety is grown and cared for exactly like the typical wine-red sweetshrub.

directions: Calycanthus floridus var. glaucus is a naturally occurring botanical variety of Carolina allspice distinguished from the typical variety by smooth, whitish-blue-green (glaucous) undersides on its leaves rather than the soft gray fuzz found on typical sweetshrub, along with a tendency toward a taller, more upright habit. It produces the same strap-petaled, spicy-fragrant, maroon-to-brownish flowers in late spring through summer, though individual plants can run somewhat paler and less deeply colored than the typical variety. Its shade tolerance, adaptability to a range of soils, and gentle suckering habit match the species, making it equally useful as a woodland-border specimen or informal hedge beneath high shade. Because leaf-underside color is the main distinguishing trait, propagate true-to-type plants from cuttings rather than seed if the glaucous foliage is the goal.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade; dwarf daphniphyllum stays much lower and more spreading than its larger relative Daphniphyllum macropodum, so it fits sites too small for the tree-sized species.

directions: Daphniphyllum humile is a smaller-scale relative of the tree-sized yuzuriha (Daphniphyllum macropodum), staying a low, mounding, spreading evergreen shrub rather than growing into a small tree, which makes it useful as a large-scale groundcover or foreground planting beneath taller shade shrubs and trees. It shares the same glossy, leathery, dark-green leaves carried on reddish petioles, with inconspicuous spring flowers and small dark fruit on female plants, and the same tolerance for deep shade that few broadleaf evergreens can match. Its lower, spreading habit and slightly better cold hardiness than the larger species make it a practical choice for filling shaded slopes or woodland-garden foregrounds where a low, textural evergreen mass is wanted. Like its larger relative, it is slow-growing, long-lived, deer-resistant, and needs little maintenance once established.
